solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 19 across to 18); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: spreading the letters out means they are scattered and laid down in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes how long a job took while spreading something about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time taken' reads like part of the surface story, but it is the definition; 'spreading' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The length of time something lasts or takes is its span, a synonym for the time taken.

parts.note: an honest person is straight, plain-dealing
flush means level, even with a surface

explanation.surface: A description of a hand, perhaps a handshake, as honest and level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is a hand of cards: in poker, five cards in sequence all of one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker a hand is the set of cards a player holds, and this is one of the strongest such combinations.

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Other people wade quickly into an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the musical direction for a fast tempo, so it serves as an adverb meaning rapidly.

clue.text: Scattered boxes on bottom of pile

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes gives spars

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down entry is its final letter

explanation.surface: Something is scattered, or boxes are stacked on the bottom of a pile.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly spread and few in number, as scattered things are.

definitions.meaning: the player judged best in a sporting fixture
the bridegroom is the man in a match, a match being a marriage

explanation.surface: A star performer described as a groom.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a match is also a marriage, and the groom is its man.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to the outstanding player in a game, and punningly the man getting married.

clue.text: Mountain in Japan, utterly fabulous, initially, to climb

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
initially says take the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A mountain in Japan is utterly fabulous to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes IJUF from 'in Japan, utterly fabulous'; 'to climb' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous volcanic peak is the highest summit in Japan.

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A colour choice for a food: yellow, or black.
explanation.definitionFit: The dairy spread churned from cream is pale yellow.

definitions.meaning: a flat inscribed slab fixed to a wall
the film of bacteria that builds up on teeth

explanation.surface: A tablet, a pill, that sticks to the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a commemorative slab on a wall and the dental deposit that a dentist scrapes off.

clue.text: Value normally expected with a soldier

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard, as in golf

explanation.surface: What one normally expects to get from a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for paratrooper, a soldier who drops in by parachute.

indicators.note: done awfully, the letters are thrown into a bad new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Conrad has a terribly cynical outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and scornful in a bitter way, close in meaning to cynical.

clue.text: One's heard on the phone offering to negotiate, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A voice on the phone offers to negotiate a deal, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound a mobile plays for an incoming call is something heard on the phone.

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone tries to catch a number as it is thrown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TEN upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a fish or a profit is to catch or gain it.

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A list of kitchen kit: an implement, also a utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is an instrument for working, a synonym in everyday use.

clue.text: Creature roaming randomly round capital in Sudan

indicators.note: round says the scrambled letters go around the other piece
randomly says the letters are put in no set order
the capital of a word is its first, capital letter

explanation.surface: An animal wanders aimlessly around the capital of Sudan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'randomly' turns ROAMING into ORGANIM, which goes 'round' S, the 'capital in Sudan', not Khartoum.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living thing, plant or animal, is a life form; a creature is one example.

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess
a nit is a foolish person in British slang

explanation.surface: A call to bring a king and a fool together.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to join closely, as broken bones or a community do.

clue.text: Very old figure kept in step

indicators.note: kept in says one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process
one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A figure, a dancer perhaps, keeps in step.
explanation.definitionFit: Used loosely of something hopelessly outdated or ancient, from the prehistoric period of stone tools.

clue.text: A sign that's confused bearing unknown proverb

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the jumbled letters hold the other piece within them
confused letters are mixed up into a different order

parts.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A road sign so muddled that its bearing is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' reworks A SIGN into SAING, and 'bearing' sets Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short well-known saying of wisdom; adage and maxim are synonyms.

indicators.note: after puts the first-named piece later in the answer

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O, and two give OO
something extended is long

explanation.surface: A long tea break after two batsmen are out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark Chinese variety of partly fermented tea.

clue.text: I had backed ally, so shockingly traitorous

indicators.note: backed means the short form is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had

indicators.note: shockingly says the letters are rearranged into a bad order

explanation.surface: Someone had backed an ally, who turned out shockingly treacherous.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaithful to a cause or friend, which is what being a traitor means.

definitions.meaning: to smooth creases from cloth with a hot press
the element Fe, a common metal

explanation.definitionFit: Both the household press for smoothing clothes and the metallic element used in steel.

clue.text: Spots all cheetahs need evidently, first of all

indicators.note: first of all says take the opening letter of every one of these words

explanation.surface: Every cheetah plainly needs its spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition of pimples, commonly just called spots in Britain.

indicators.note: hugging says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a penny is an example of a coin

explanation.surface: Penny, a woman, embraces an American relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a name; it is the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The child of an aunt or uncle is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Insect in a pickle? Most delightful

indicators.note: in a pickle means in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An insect in a jar of pickle: hardly the most delightful thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective for pleasant, so the most pleasing of all.
